name: PixiTween Director C1: catalog runner from the UI (CSV in, verified wall, $0 price edit)
description: Runs the S19 catalogue path from the studio: import a CSV (or the demo feed), build one verified 9:16 retail clip per product in the background, show a live wall with a status and check chip per row and one player, and edit a price with a $0 rebuild. Leaves out showrunner planning, a Spark price read, Publish/MP4, the product page and variant line films.

userStories.title: Catalog run contracts and the catalog.row / catalog.done events
userStories.description: As a catalog builder, I want one typed shape for a catalog run and its rows so that the server, the events and the wall agree.
steps: Read docs/architecture/catalog-runner.md (Row states), shared/catalog.ts (productSchema) and shared/events.ts (the discriminated union and the `base` fields).

Create shared/catalog-run.ts exporting zod schemas and inferred types: ROW_STATUSES = ['queued','cutting','building','checking','ready','fixed','flagged','failed'] as const; rowStatusSchema; rowCheckSchema = { ok: boolean, rounds: int >= 1, applied: string[], blocking: string[] (each 'KIND subject'), warnings: string[] }.

In shared/catalog-run.ts add catalogRowSchema = { product: productSchema, status: rowStatusSchema, look?: string, why?: string, accent?: string, clipVersion: int >= 0 (default 0), check: rowCheckSchema.nullable() (default null), error?: string, ms?: number } and catalogRunSchema = { id: string matching /^cat_[a-z0-9]{8,32}$/, filmId: string, aspect: enum '9:16'|'16:9'|'1:1', createdAt: string, state: enum 'running'|'done', costUsd: number >= 0, rows: catalogRowSchema[] (1..200) }.

Export helpers: newCatalogId() returning 'cat_' plus 12 lowercase hex chars (node-free: use crypto.getRandomValues), isFinal(status) (true for ready, fixed, flagged, failed), and summarize(rows) returning { total, final, ready, fixed, flagged, failed }.

In shared/events.ts add two union members only: { ...base, type: 'catalog.row', catalogId: string, row: catalogRowSchema } and { ...base, type: 'catalog.done', catalogId: string, costUsd: number, ms: number }. Import catalogRowSchema from './catalog-run'.

Create shared/catalog-run.test.ts: a valid run parses; a bad id ('x1') fails; summarize on one row of each final status plus one queued returns total 5, final 4; filmEventSchema parses a catalog.row event built with makeEvent.
acceptanceCriteria: catalogRunSchema.parse accepts a run with id 'cat_0123456789ab' and one queued row, and rejects id 'x1'
isFinal('fixed') is true and isFinal('checking') is false
filmEventSchema.safeParse of a catalog.row event made with makeEvent returns success: true
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Catalog run store on disk with atomic row updates
userStories.description: As a runner, I want catalog runs and their clips stored on disk so that the wall survives a reload and a price edit can rebuild a clip.
steps: Read shared/catalog-run.ts (US-001) and server/store/film-store.ts (how it writes JSON atomically under a data dir).

Create server/catalog/run-store.ts exporting createRunStore({ dir }) where dir is the data dir; runs live in <dir>/catalogs/<id>/run.json, clips in <dir>/catalogs/<id>/clips/<productId>.json, build inputs in <dir>/catalogs/<id>/build/<productId>.json.

Methods: create(run) writes run.json (throws if it exists); get(id) returns the parsed run or undefined; list() returns runs newest first (by createdAt); updateRow(id, productId, patch) merges the patch into that row, validates with catalogRowSchema, writes atomically (write to run.json.tmp then rename) and returns the new row; setRun(id, patch) for state and costUsd.

Methods for files: saveClip(id, productId, comp) and readClip(id, productId); saveBuild(id, productId, input) and readBuild(id, productId). Each saveClip increments the row's clipVersion through updateRow.
Serialize writes per run id with a simple promise chain (a Map<string, Promise<void>>) so two updateRow calls never lose an update.
Validate productId against /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/ before using it in a path; throw RangeError otherwise.

Create server/catalog/run-store.test.ts with a mkdtemp dir: create then get round-trips; 20 parallel updateRow calls on different rows all land; saveClip twice gives clipVersion 2; productId '../x' throws RangeError; list() orders two runs newest first.
acceptanceCriteria: After 20 concurrent updateRow calls on 20 rows, get(id) shows all 20 patches
saveClip twice on one row leaves clipVersion === 2 and readClip returns the second comp
updateRow with productId '../x' throws RangeError and writes nothing outside <dir>/catalogs
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Photo resolution and the cut-out cache
userStories.description: As a runner, I want each feed image_link turned into photo bytes safely, and each photo cut out once, so that a repeat run of the demo costs nothing.
steps: Read docs/architecture/catalog-runner.md (Photos, Caching) and fixtures/catalog/feed-6.csv (image_link values are repo paths).
Create server/catalog/photos.ts exporting resolvePhoto(link, uploads: Map<string, Buffer>, repoRoot = process.cwd()): Buffer | { error: string }.

Order: an upload whose key equals path.basename(link) wins; else if link starts with http:// or https:// return { error: 'remote photos are not supported yet' }; else if link is absolute, contains '..', or does not start with 'fixtures/' or 'data/assets/' return { error: `photo not found: ${link}` }; else read the file under repoRoot if it exists, else the same not-found error.

In the same file export photoKey(bytes) = sha256 hex of the bytes, and createCutoutCache(dir) with get(key) and set(key, { id, width, height, accent, chroma }) persisted in <dir>/catalogs/cutouts.json (read once, written after each set).

Create server/catalog/photos.test.ts: an upload named 'can.png' wins over a repo path 'fixtures/s13/can-product.png'; 'fixtures/s13/can-product.png' resolves with no upload; '../etc/passwd', '/etc/passwd' and 'https://x.test/a.png' return the stated errors; cache set then a new createCutoutCache on the same dir returns the entry.
acceptanceCriteria: resolvePhoto('fixtures/s13/can-product.png', new Map()) returns a Buffer whose length equals the file size
resolvePhoto('../secret.png', new Map()) returns { error: 'photo not found: ../secret.png' } and reads no file
A cut-out cached in one createCutoutCache instance is returned by a second instance on the same dir
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Art adapters: real SAM and Muse plate, and a free fake for tests
userStories.description: As a runner, I want the paid art steps behind one small interface so that tests, e2e and DIRECTOR_FAKE runs are offline and free.
steps: Read server/art/cutout.ts (cutout signature and return), server/art/stills.ts (generateLookPlate), server/art/palette.ts (dominantAccent) and the cut-out and plate parts of scripts/live/s19-catalog.ts.

Create server/catalog/art.ts exporting interface CatalogArt { cut(bytes: Buffer, noun: string): Promise<{ id: string; width: number; height: number; accent: string; chroma: number; usd: number }>; plate(look: LookId, occasion: OccasionId, noun: string, aspect: Aspect): Promise<{ id: string; width: number; height: number; usd: number }> }.

Export realArt(ctx: ToolCtx, assets: AssetStore & { get(id): Promise<AssetRef> }): cut calls cutout(ctx, { source: bytes, noun, sceneId: 'catalog' }), reads the cut-out bytes back from the asset store to run dominantAccent, and returns usd 0.0025; plate calls generateLookPlate(ctx, { look, occasion, productClass: `${noun}s`, aspect, sceneId: look }) and returns usd 0.01.

Export fakeArt(assets) with counters calls.cut and calls.plate: cut trims the photo with sharp().trim(), stores it as a PNG asset with role 'cutout', and returns accent from dominantAccent and usd 0; plate stores a flat 720x1280 PNG (sharp create, background '#d9cbb5') with role 'plate' and returns usd 0.

Create server/catalog/art.test.ts using makeTestFilm from server/test-utils/film.ts: fakeArt.cut on fixtures/s13/can-product.png returns width and height > 0 and an asset that the store can read; fakeArt.plate returns width 720, height 1280; counters count each call. Do not test realArt against a network.
acceptanceCriteria: fakeArt(assets).cut(canPng, 'can') resolves with usd 0, width > 0, and an asset id readable from the asset store
After one cut and two plate calls, fake.calls equals { cut: 1, plate: 2 }
server/catalog/art.ts imports cutout and generateLookPlate from server/art and does not reimplement them (grep finds no 'segment' or image-generation HTTP call in it)

`npm test` passes (offline, no network)

userStories.title: Build one row: look, clip, verifier verdict (pure of paid calls)
userStories.description: As a runner, I want one function that turns a product plus its cut-out and plate into a saved clip and a row verdict, so that the first build and every price edit share it.
steps: Read server/authoring/verify-clip.ts (verifyRetailClip returns { ok, comp, input, rounds }; rounds[i] has groups, warnings, applied), server/authoring/catalog-clip.ts (buildCatalogClip, CatalogClipInput) and shared/catalog-run.ts.

Create server/catalog/row.ts exporting type RowBuild = CatalogClipInput & { plateMap?: unknown } (the exact input, stored per row) and buildRow(build: RowBuild): { comp, check: RowCheck | null, status: 'ready' | 'fixed' | 'flagged', build: RowBuild }.
For look 'hero-3d' call buildCatalogClip(build) and return status 'ready', check null.

For any other look call verifyRetailClip with { aspect, look, plate (with map: plateMap when present), product, title, price, wasPrice, currency, brand, accent, baseY }. Map the result: check = { ok, rounds: rounds.length, applied: all rounds' applied joined, blocking: last round's groups as `${kind} ${subject}`, warnings: last round's warnings as `${kind} ${subject}` (first 5) }. status = !ok ? 'flagged' : rounds.length > 1 ? 'fixed' : 'ready'. Return the verifier's comp, and build with baseY set from result.input.baseY when the fixer changed it.
Export loadPlateMap(plateId, root = process.cwd()) reading fixtures/plates/<plateId>.json when it exists (its surfaces, busy, quadrants), else undefined.

Create server/catalog/row.test.ts with plain ClipAsset fixtures (no art calls): a tabletop-hero row with the plate map from fixtures/plates/ast_04d50dc418756070b185948227520d4f.json is 'ready' with rounds 1; the same row with baseY 0.5 is 'fixed' and check.applied[0] starts with 'baseY 0.5 ->'; the returned build.baseY is the fixed value; a price-promo row (no plate) returns a comp and a check.
acceptanceCriteria: buildRow on the tabletop-hero fixture with baseY 0.5 returns status 'fixed', check.rounds 2 and check.applied[0] matching /^baseY 0\.5 -> /
buildRow on the same fixture without baseY returns status 'ready' and check.blocking []
buildRow called twice on the same build returns deep-equal comps (deterministic)
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Catalog runner: per photo, per product, events and cost
userStories.description: As a shop owner, I want every product of my feed built in the background with live progress so that the wall fills while I watch.
steps: Read scripts/live/s19-catalog.ts lines 55-125 (the order: distinct photos -> cut-out -> prepareRound -> pickLook -> plate -> accent -> clip), server/catalog/row.ts, run-store.ts, photos.ts and art.ts.

Create server/catalog/runner.ts exporting runCatalog(o: { run: CatalogRun; store: RunStore; art: CatalogArt; assets: AssetStore; uploads: Map<string, Buffer>; cutCache; plates: { get(key): PlateRef | undefined; set(key, ref): void }; emit(e: { type: 'catalog.row' | 'catalog.done', ... }): void; now?: () => number }): Promise<void>.

Port from s19: NOUN = { drinks: 'can', home: 'mug' } (else 'product'); one cut per distinct photo (resolvePhoto, then cutCache by photoKey, else art.cut and cache it; add usd to cost); prepareRound per photo; pickLook per product; plate key `${look}:${noun}` from plates, else art.plate (skip for hero-3d and looks whose LOOKS[look].plate is null); accent as in s19 accentOf (photo accent when chroma > 0.05, else '#3d4a5c').

Row transitions, each saved with store.updateRow and emitted as catalog.row: cutting when its photo is being cut, building, checking, then the buildRow status. Save the clip (store.saveClip) and the build (store.saveBuild) before the final transition. Plate map: loadPlateMap(plate.id).
A row whose photo fails or whose build throws becomes 'failed' with error (first 200 chars); the run continues with the next row.
At the end: setRun state 'done' and costUsd, then emit catalog.done with costUsd and ms.

Create server/catalog/runner.test.ts with makeTestFilm stores, a temp run store, fakeArt and fixtures/catalog/feed-6.csv parsed with parseFeed: all 6 rows end final; fake.calls.cut === 2 (two distinct photos); a second run with the same cutCache makes 0 cut calls; a row with image_link 'fixtures/nope.png' ends 'failed' while the others finish; events include one catalog.done.
acceptanceCriteria: On feed-6 with fakeArt every row ends in ready, fixed, flagged or failed and exactly one catalog.done is emitted
fakeArt.calls.cut is 2 on the first run and 0 on a second run sharing the cut-out cache
A product with image_link 'fixtures/nope.png' ends status 'failed' with error 'photo not found: fixtures/nope.png' and the other 5 rows still finish

`npm test` passes (offline, no network)

userStories.title: Catalog HTTP routes: import, read, list, clip
userStories.description: As a studio, I want routes to start a catalog run from a CSV or the demo feed and read its rows and clips so that the UI never needs the CLI.
steps: Read server/http/handlers/films.ts (parseBody, InputError, makeToolCtx, films.create), server/http/routes.ts and server/catalog/runner.ts.

Create server/http/handlers/catalogs.ts exporting registerCatalogRoutes(app, deps, opts?: { art?: (ctx) => CatalogArt }). Default art: fakeArt when process.env.DIRECTOR_FAKE === '1', else realArt(ctx, deps.assets); if no fake and loadEnv().metaApiKey is empty, POST answers 503 { error: 'meta_key_missing' }.

POST /api/catalogs (multipart): `csv` (file or text) or `demo=feed-6` (reads fixtures/catalog/feed-6.csv); `photos` (zero or more files, keyed by file name); `aspect` (default '9:16'). parseFeed errors -> 400 { error: 'bad_feed', errors }. More than 50 products -> 400 { error: 'too_many_products' }.

On success: films.create({ aspect, title: `Catalog: ${n} products`, brief: { text: 'Catalog run', productAssetId: '' }, assets: [] }); create the run (all rows queued) in the run store under deps.dataDir ?? loadEnv().DATA_DIR; start runCatalog without awaiting it (catch and log errors; emit through makeToolCtx(film.id).emit); plates: with real art, backed by web/public/cartoon/look-plates.json (read; write after a new plate); with fake art, an in-memory Map so tests and e2e never write fake plate ids into that file (opts.platesFile overrides the path). Return 202 { catalogId, filmId }.
GET /api/catalogs -> { runs: [{ id, filmId, createdAt, state, total, final }] }; GET /api/catalogs/:id -> the run or 404; GET /api/catalogs/:id/clips/:productId -> the clip JSON or 404.
Add one line to server/http/routes.ts: registerCatalogRoutes(app, deps).

Create server/http/handlers/catalogs.test.ts with app.request against a Hono app built like server/http/app.test.ts, art injected as fakeArt: demo=feed-6 returns 202 and, after awaiting until the run's state is 'done' (poll the store, max 10 s), GET returns 6 final rows; a CSV missing the price column returns 400 bad_feed; an unknown id returns 404.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/catalogs with demo=feed-6 returns 202 with catalogId matching /^cat_/ and a filmId
POST with csv 'id,title\nx,y' returns 400 with error 'bad_feed' and errors naming the missing columns
GET /api/catalogs/:id/clips/:productId returns a composition with fps and durationInFrames once that row is final

`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Price edit: PATCH a product, rebuild its clip at $0
userStories.description: As a shop owner, I want to change a price on the wall and have the ad update in about a second for nothing, so that a catalog stays live.
steps: Read server/http/handlers/catalogs.ts (US-007), server/catalog/row.ts (buildRow, RowBuild) and run-store.ts (readBuild, saveClip, updateRow).

In server/http/handlers/catalogs.ts add PATCH /api/catalogs/:id/products/:productId with JSON { price?: number >= 0, salePrice?: number >= 0 | null, title?: string 1..120 }. Validate with zod; 400 { error: 'bad_edit' } on failure; 404 for an unknown run or product; 409 { error: 'not_ready' } while the row is not final or is 'failed'.

Apply to the stored product: new price/salePrice/title. Build input: readBuild, then set build.title, build.price = shownPrice(product) and build.wasPrice = product.salePrice !== undefined ? product.price : undefined.
Time it with performance.now(): buildRow(build), saveClip, saveBuild, updateRow with the new product, status, check and ms; emit catalog.row through the carrier film's ctx. Return 200 { row }.
Never call art, cutout, generateLookPlate or any model in this route.

fakeArt calls.cut and calls.plate are unchanged by the PATCH

userStories.title: End-to-end: demo feed to a full wall and a price edit, in the browser
userStories.description: As an owner, I want one browser test of the whole catalog flow on fake art so that the demo path cannot silently break.
steps: Read playwright.config.ts (the server runs with DIRECTOR_FAKE=1), an existing spec under e2e/ for the page-open pattern, and web/src/catalog/CatalogImport.tsx / CatalogWall.tsx test ids.

Create e2e/catalog-runner.spec.ts: open the studio, click the rail tab 'Catalog', click 'Use demo feed (6 products)', expect the URL to contain ?catalog=cat_, then wait (timeout 60 s) until the wall header starts with '6/6 done'.

Click the 'Stone Mug' row; expect the player canvas to be visible; untick 'on sale', type 21 in its price input and press Enter; expect the row to show '$21.00' (it started at '$19.00', on sale from $24.00) and the text 'updated in' within 5 s.
Save a screenshot to debug/app/catalog-runner.png and assert the browser console has no error containing 'WebGL' or 'context lost'.
Update docs/misc/todos/CATALOG-CREW.md: a 'C1 catalog runner (UI)' section with the built pieces and the three manual gates from this PRD; do not tick the gates.
acceptanceCriteria: `npm run e2e -- e2e/catalog-runner.spec.ts` passes: 6/6 rows final and the Stone Mug row shows '$21.00' after the edit
debug/app/catalog-runner.png exists after the run and the console check finds no WebGL context-lost error
docs/misc/todos/CATALOG-CREW.md has a C1 section listing MG-1, MG-2 and MG-3 unticked
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes
Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

readFirst: docs/architecture/catalog-runner.md (the whole spec: design, row states, what to reuse)
scripts/live/s19-catalog.ts (the logic the runner ports: cut-outs, prepareRound, pickLook, plates, accent, buildCatalogClip)
server/authoring/verify-clip.ts (verifyRetailClip, its result shape) and server/authoring/catalog-clip.ts
shared/catalog.ts (parseFeed, Product, shownPrice, formatPrice) and shared/events.ts (the FilmEvent union)
server/http/handlers/films.ts (multipart parse, films.create, makeToolCtx) and server/test-utils/film.ts (temp stores for tests)
web/src/App.tsx (tabs and the ?film= routing), web/src/api/sse.ts (useFilmEvents), web/src/player/Player.tsx
metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.

Shared edits are small: shared/events.ts gets only the catalog.row and catalog.done members; server/http/routes.ts only the registerCatalogRoutes line; web/src/App.tsx only the Catalog tab and the ?catalog= route; docs/misc/todos/CATALOG-CREW.md only a C1 section.

Reuse, never copy: parseFeed, cutout, dominantAccent, generateLookPlate, pickLook, LOOKS, prepareRound, buildCatalogClip and verifyRetailClip are imported from where they live. Do not edit those files.

Tests and e2e never call SAM or Muse: the runner takes an injected `art` object, and tests pass the fake art from server/catalog/art.ts. The real art is only constructed when DIRECTOR_FAKE is not set.

Never invent a check result. A row's chip shows exactly what verifyRetailClip returned (rounds, applied, blocking kinds). If a clip passes in round 1, it is `ready`; do not stage a fault to show a catch.
A price edit never calls cut, plate, SAM, Muse or any language model: it rebuilds from the row's stored build input. A test asserts the fake art call counters do not move.

`npm test` has known failures outside your files (server/llm/glimmer/docs.test.ts needs docs/local-mode.md; occasionally server/review/loop.test.ts or server/http/handlers/review.test.ts flake under load and pass on rerun). Do not edit those files; the gate passes when no other test fails.
The dev server on http://localhost:5173 is owner-run and shared: never kill or restart it. If it is down, run the browser check with `npm run e2e -- e2e/catalog-runner.spec.ts` instead.

ui: Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

manualGates: MG-1: owner runs the studio with real keys (`npm run dev`), opens the Catalog tab, clicks 'Use demo feed (6 products)' and watches 6 rows reach ready/fixed/flagged. First run spends about $0.02 (SAM cut-outs for 2 photos, plates only for looks missing from look-plates.json); a second run must show $0.00.
MG-2: owner edits one price on the wall (24.00 -> 19.00) three times, stopwatches Enter to new price on screen, and records the median next to the server `ms` the tile shows.
MG-3: owner plays 3 clips from the wall in Chrome and scores how they look (1-5).
